identity.title: Clumping and the Interpretation of kpc-scale Maps of the Interstellar Medium: Smooth H I and Clumpy, Variable H<SUB>2</SUB> Surface Density

paper_type_evidence.quote: This includes the MAGMA (cite: WONG11) and NANTEN (cite: FUKUI99) surveys of the LMC, the IRAM 30-m survey of CO in M31 (cite: NIETEN06)
ALMA science verification data on the Antennae galaxies

question.value: How do kpc-scale (area-weighted) surface densities of H I and CO-traced H2 relate to mass-weighted cloud-scale surface densities, as quantified by a clumping factor?

evidence.quote: We define a “clumping factor” that captures this translation as the ratio of the mass-weighted surface density, which is often the quantity of physical interest, to the area-weighted surface density, which is observed.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00003.SV.
the Antennae data target the CO $J=3\rightarrow2$ and CO $J=2\rightarrow1$ transitions
the Antennae data target the CO $J=3\rightarrow2$ and CO $J=2\rightarrow1$ transitions

other_facilities.name: THINGS, LITTLE THINGS, VLA ANGST (H I)

provided.value: High-resolution H I integrated intensity maps

evidence.quote: We make use of three recent H I surveys of nearby galaxies: THINGS (cite: WALTER08), LITTLE THINGS (cite: HUNTER12), and VLA ANGST (cite: OTT12).

other_facilities.name: MAGMA, NANTEN, IRAM 30-m, BIMA+FCRAO, BIMA SONG, CARMA, PAWS (CO)

provided.value: CO J=1-0 maps of LMC, M31, M33, M51 and other nearby galaxies

evidence.quote: Except for the ALMA Antennae data, all of these data sets target the CO $J=1\rightarrow0$ line and include (sometimes exclusively) short-spacing data

what.value: Composite CO survey of the Milky Way

evidence.quote: we also calculate $c$ from the composite CO survey of the Milky Way by (cite: DAME01)

masking.value: Noise from empty regions; core of two successive channels with S/N>5, expanded to fainter emission

evidence.quote: often two successive channels with $S/N > 5$ and expand this high significance core to include fainter but still significant emission

smoothing.value: Gaussian kernel to 1 kpc; LMC and M33 convolved to slightly worse resolution before masking

evidence.quote: To calculate $\left< \Sigma \right>^{\rm A}$, we smooth from the native resolution to 1 kpc using a normalized Gaussian kernel.

unstated_but_needed: Exact mask expansion threshold for CO
ALMA Antennae calibration, imaging and array details, and whether short spacings were included
Kernel width and sampling details for the 1 kpc smoothing and the criterion for the sensitivity-based region selection
Final per-dataset masks and convolved resolutions for LMC and M33

method.value: Mask cubes using noise estimated from empty regions and a high-significance core, then integrate to moment 0

evidence.quote: We integrate the masked data cube to produce a moment 0 map, which we use in further analysis.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute area- and mass-weighted surface density and clumping factor at 1 kpc

method.value: Smooth Sigma to 1 kpc for the area-weighted value; smooth Sigma^2 and divide by the area-weighted value for the mass-weighted value; c is their ratio, sampled at hexagonal Nyquist points

evidence.quote: we calculate $\Sigma^2$ at the native resolution, convolve this map to 1 kpc resolution using a normalized Gaussian kernel, and then divide that map by $\left< \Sigma \right>^{\rm A}$

assumptions.value: Sigma proportional to I; alpha_CO = 4.35 Msun pc^-2 (K km/s)^-1; N(HI) = 1.823e18 I_HI

evidence.quote: adopting a fixed $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 4.35$ M$_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$ (K km s$^{-1}$)$^{-1}$

validation.value: Footnote test adding a faint diffuse CO component to PAWS M51 lowers c from ~6 to ~5.1

evidence.quote: then $c$ drops from $\approx 6$ to $\approx 5.1$ over the region that we consider.

results_numeric.quantity: Median CO clumping factor across data sets

evidence.quote: The median among all data sets is $\approx 7$ with a factor of $2$–$3$ rms scatter among measurements.

findings_qualitative.value: H I is smooth; CO is clumpy and variable, so kpc H2/H I ratios do not translate to cloud-scale ratios

evidence.quote: As a result, the ratio H$_2$/H I measured at $\sim$ kpc resolution cannot be trivially interpreted as a cloud-scale ratio of surface densities.

claims.hypothesis: H I and H2 have similar clumping
claims.experiment: Compute c at 1 kpc from high-resolution H I and CO maps
claims.result: H I c~1.3; CO median c~7
claims.finding: Molecular gas is far more clumped than atomic gas

evidence.quote: The median clumping factor for a CO data set is $c=7$, while the median clumping factor for an H I data set is $c=1.26$.

claims.hypothesis: CO arises from clouds with universal mass-weighted surface density
claims.experiment: Compare mass-weighted surface density versus area-weighted
claims.finding: No good evidence for a fixed value, though not conclusive

evidence.quote: The figure provides no good evidence that CO emerges from a fixed $\left< \Sigma \right>^{\rm M}$ at high spatial resolution.

limitations_admitted.value: CO data are scarce and heterogeneous; masking removes faint diffuse emission

evidence.quote: This scarcity leads us to assemble a heterogeneous collection of high resolution CO.

referee_caveats_inferred: Heterogeneous CO resolutions and sensitivities make c comparisons across datasets uncertain
Masking choices affect the Sigma^2 term

data_public_as_stated.value: Several surveys public; CARMA M31 and PAWS data unpublished at the time

evidence.quote: We acknowledge the BIMA SONG, LITTLE THINGS, and VLA ANGST collaborations for making their data public.

missing_for_reproduction: Unpublished CARMA M31 and PAWS data
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB across all surveys; ALMA SV Antennae portion a few GB
reproducibility.score_reason: Method and equations are clear and many data are public, but heterogeneous data and masking details are underspecified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe depends on many heterogeneous datasets with incompletely specified masks.
